newsitem.title: IRAN: Family murders by teenage lovers shock Iran.
newsitem.headline: Family murders by teenage lovers shock Iran.

text.p: Iranians have been shocked by a case in which two 16-year-old lovers confessed to choking to death two younger members of the girl's rich family and trying to kill her mother, apparently for opposing their marriage.

The crimes, uncovered last week, sparked an outcry over youth problems in Iran, an issue often debated in the strict Moslem country where some 70 percent of the country's 60 million people are below 30 years of age.

"Everyone I know is shocked," a high school teacher said. "I do expect bizarre things from youngsters, not exactly murder though. They are assertive and answer back to teachers. It was not so when I was young."

"Many youths seem to have little hope for their future, ready to do anything to secure a desired future," he said, citing press reports that the rich girl and her middle class boyfriend had plotted to win her family's wealth.
Most Iranian media blamed Western culture -- through contraband video films and satellite television -- and urged parents to exert more control over their children.
"We used to get news about small and big killers mostly from the West, with its lost young generation. But why in our country which is so rich with spirituality?" asked Akhbar daily.

The crimes also suggested a Western lifestyle because they were committed by youngsters having close relations outside of marriage -- something strictly banned by Iran's Islamic laws, newspapers suggested.
"Our youth is suspended between fading old values, lack of new ones...and a frightening generation gap," Iran daily said.
Iranian television broadcast and then replayed a lengthy programme on the murders, carried out in one of the wealthiest neighbourhoods of the capital.
Tehran police chief Brigadier General Youssef Reza Abolfathi told the programme: "It is not really the first case, we have had a few others."
He was apparently referring to a case last year in which a 16-year-old girl and her 18-year-old lover confessed to killing four members of her family for blocking their marriage.
"Families should not allow the satanic satellite and the vulgarity of Western culture to enter their homes. Parents should supervise their children more," Abolfathi said.
But an Iranian journalist blamed high financial demands by parents on the groom before they let their daughters get married.

"Getting married is becoming an impossible dream for many young men because the girl's family often demands that he should have an apartment and a good job," he told Reuters. "They do not think of the high rents and the shape of the job market."
